strongest_valid_partial_result: The candidate rigorously verifies that the standard simplex attains the conjectured general Mahler value and the cube attains the conjectured symmetric Mahler value, with complete proofs of affine invariance, Santaló point covariance, and explicit volume computations.
fatal_gaps: Does not prove the general Mahler lower bound for arbitrary convex bodies
Does not prove the symmetric Mahler lower bound for centrally symmetric bodies
Does not classify equality cases (only verifies the conjectured extremizers attain the values)
Does not address the functional Mahler inequalities
Does not prove Gromov width 4 for symmetric polar products
evidence_quotes: The general lower bounds and the full equality characterizations of the Mahler conjectures are not proved here
This proves the 'if' direction of the equality case in Part A. It does not prove the lower bound for non-simplicial bodies, nor the 'only if' characterization
No counterexample is constructed, so the conjectures are neither proved nor disproved here
notes: The candidate manuscript is mathematically rigorous but explicitly proves only that the conjectured extremizers (simplices and cubes) attain the conjectured Mahler values. It does not prove the actual Mahler conjectures, which require establishing the lower bounds for all convex bodies and classifying equality cases. The manuscript honestly labels itself as PARTIAL and lists the unproved statements. The work that is presented—affine invariance, Santaló point covariance, simplex polar computation, and cube polar computation—is correct and complete, but represents only verification of the extremizers, not resolution of the conjectures.
